description: phaethon is a Go installer that gives every agent harness on a machine its own computers: it bundles hollow (KVM VM desks) and bangboo (agent MCP tools), registers bangboo with installed harnesses, installs the usage skill, and provisions Linux hosts over ssh. For developers running Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor and similar apps who need self-hosted agent computers.
features: One install bundles hollow, bangboo binaries and agent skill
Registers bangboo MCP server with every installed agent harness
Installs phaethon skill into harness skill folders via bmo
Provisions any ssh-reachable KVM Linux machine as VM host
Adds already-serving hosts by connect code (a hollow, or another machine's desktop as NAME/desktop); sync/doctor leave served desktops alone
Serves local real desktop with share, trust CIDR, view-only
Runs bangboo gateway embedded in apps with in-memory token
Ships without cloning: importable Go packages, an npm SDK carrying the bangboo binary and <phaethon-desk>, and v* releases (GitHub tarballs, Homebrew tap, install.sh)
Upgrades hollow on hosts and rebuilds missing Linux images
Manages hosts: add, list, scan, remove, uninstall over ssh
Proxies bangboo secret storage and live desk browser view
Doctor command verifies binaries, harnesses, hosts end-to-end
Syncs local install, registrations, skill and all hosts
Uninstall removes binaries, harness registrations and skill
Passes bangboo gateway (embed desks in other apps) and local (the desktop you sit at, shared with agents for a while) through as phaethon commands

layers.name: Bundle
layers.what: embed.FS carrying hollow+bangboo binaries, versions.json, skills; payload extraction

layers.name: Local install
layers.what: Writes bangboo/hollow binaries to binDir, tracks changes, PATH handling

layers.name: Harness registration
layers.what: Detects Claude Code/Codex/Gemini/Cursor/Desktop/OpenCode, registers/unregisters bangboo MCP server, backs up configs

layers.name: Host provisioning
layers.what: managed hosts.json state, ssh setup, hollow service install, URL discovery

layers.name: Sync and health
layers.what: phaethon sync/doctor/scan via bangboo host ls JSON, upgrades, image rebuilds

layers.name: Runtime
layers.what: Go 1.26, macOS/Linux client; x86_64 Linux KVM hosts; ssh, QEMU, makima/Tailscale/WireGuard networking

flows.name: Install computers
steps: skill install via bmo or copy (skills/phaethon/)

flows.name: Add host
steps: phaethon host add MACHINE or connect code (hosts.go)
remote ssh (remote.go) or bangboo host add code
send hollow-linux-amd64, install service + QEMU or register served desktop
build Linux image once for VM hosts

flows.name: Keep current
steps: upgrade hollow, rebuild outdated images, leave served desktops alone

flows.name: Agent uses desk
steps: hollow host serves VM desks, local serve shares real desktop

layout: main.go — CLI entrypoint, usage and subcommand dispatch
bundle.go — embedded bundle FS, versions.json, payload extraction
install.go — local binary install, binDir/stateDir helpers
jsonedit.go — in-place JSON/JSONC config edits preserving formatting
tomledit.go — in-place Codex TOML edits preserving formatting
hosts.go — host add/ls/rm state in hosts.json
remote.go — ssh-only remote execution, local-machine path
sync.go — sync/doctor/scan via bangboo host ls JSON
hosts_test.go, config_test.go — unit tests for host settings and config edits
bundle/ — carried hollow-linux-amd64, hollow+bangboo client binaries, versions.json
skills/phaethon/ — agent skill teaching desk tool use
versions.env — the hollow and bangboo tags a release is built from (HOLLOW_REF, BANGBOO_REF)
install.sh — curl | sh installer: detects os/arch, verifies SHA256SUMS, installs to ~/.local/bin
scripts/formula.sh, .github/workflows/ — the Homebrew formula from a release's SHA256SUMS; CI, and the v* release (tarballs, GitHub release, tap)
run: make — build hollow+bangboo, bundle, install, run phaethon install
make build — produce ./build/phaethon with bundled binaries
make update — rebuild everything then phaethon sync hosts
phaethon install — install binaries, register harnesses, install skill
phaethon host add MACHINE / host ls / scan / host rm — manage hosts
phaethon sync / phaethon doctor --deep — update all, verify end-to-end
phaethon uninstall — remove binaries, registrations, skill
make dist — dist/phaethon-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz and SHA256SUMS for this platform; HOLLOW_REF/BANGBOO_REF (versions.env) pin the sources
brew install justin06lee/tap/phaethon, or curl -fsSL …/phaethon/master/install.sh | sh — install without cloning, once a release exists
conventions: Build with Go 1.26+; hollow/bangboo built by their own Makefiles from ../ or .cache/
Never fetch at install time: everything installed is carried in embed bundle/
Keep first harness config version as *.before-phaethon
Use harness add-command where available, edit config file otherwise

cli.summary: CLI layer is the Go entrypoint that wires every phaethon operation together: install, host add/ls/rm, sync, doctor, scan, secret, view, gateway, local, uninstall. It now splits dispatch across main.go plus hosts.go and sync.go, parsing subcommands/flags including host add via connect code and delegating to Bundle, Local install, Harness, Host, and Sync layers. Newcomers must grasp it owns no logic itself — it is dispatch plus usage text and exit codes, and served desktops (NAME/desktop) are left alone by sync/doctor.

map.name: CLI usage text and version flag

flows.name: Run any subcommand
steps: report error and set exit code

files: main.go — Go entrypoint; usage text, flag/subcommand dispatch, delegation to all other layers
hosts.go — host subcommand handling including add via connect code for served desktops
sync.go — sync/doctor handling that leaves served desktops alone
rules: Keep CLI files dispatch-only; implement behavior in the owning layer, not here
edges: Bundle — install path pulls embedded binaries/versions/skills it carries
Local install — install/uninstall path writes/removes bangboo/hollow binaries
Harness registration — install path registers bangboo MCP with detected harnesses
Host provisioning — host add/ls/rm path manages hosts.json and remote hollow setup
Sync and health — sync/doctor/scan path queries hosts via bangboo host ls JSON

bundle.summary: The Bundle layer is phaethon's self-contained install payload: an embed.FS carrying hollow+bangboo binaries, versions.json, and skills, so install requires no network fetch. It is built by make next to hollow and bangboo checkouts and read via helpers in bundle.go. A newcomer must grasp that if a payload is missing the binary was mis-built, not mis-downloaded.

flows.name: Read an embedded payload
steps: Call payload(name) to read bundle/<name> from embed.FS
Return missing-build error if not embedded

files: bundle.go — embed.FS (bundle+skills), versions.json reading, payload() / localName() / sha helpers
rules: Never fetch payloads from the network here; installing phaethon is the whole install.
Build with make next to hollow and bangboo checkouts or payload() fails with a build error.
Binary names are OS/arch-qualified via localName(); do not hardcode them.
skills/phaethon/SKILL.md must stay in step with bangboo's tools: it teaches the rules for the user's own desktop (local/desktop, shared with bangboo local share); change both together
edges: Local install — consumes extracted binaries written to binDir
Host provisioning — consumes embedded Linux hollow payload for remote hosts
Harness registration — consumes embedded skill content taught to agents

local-install.summary: This layer installs the bangboo and hollow binaries beside phaethon in binDir and reports what changed so repeat installs are no-ops. It resolves binary paths by preferring binDir then falling back to PATH lookup. Newcomers must grasp: writes are content-addressed by SHA — identical binaries are skipped, never blindly overwritten.

flows.name: Install binaries
steps: Load embedded payload per program (bangboo, hollow)
Compare fileSHA of existing file to payload SHA and skip if equal

files: install.go — writes bangboo/hollow binaries to binDir, SHA-skips unchanged files, resolves binary paths with PATH fallback
install.sh — curl | sh installer for phaethon itself: os/arch, the latest or PHAETHON_VERSION release, SHA256SUMS check, ~/.local/bin or $PREFIX/bin; must run under dash
versions.env — the hollow and bangboo tags a release is built from
.github/workflows/release.yml — v* tag: per-platform tarballs, GitHub release with SHA256SUMS, Homebrew formula via scripts/formula.sh pushed to the tap
rules: Never rewrite a binary whose SHA already matches — repeat install must report no change.
Always install bangboo and hollow together beside phaethon in binDir; do not split locations.
Path lookup must prefer binDir first, then PATH via exec.LookPath.
Emit user messages to stderr via say, not stdout.
binDir() skips Homebrew's Cellar (packaged() in bundle.go): run from brew, bangboo and hollow go to ~/.local/bin, since brew upgrade deletes the Cellar version and harnesses would point at nothing
A release builds hollow and bangboo from the tags in versions.env (cloned into .cache, GOWORK=off), never sibling checkouts; never pass VERSION= to make, it reaches their Makefiles too
edges: Bundle — payload bytes and versions for bangboo/hollow come from embedded bundle
CLI — install command drives installBinaries and reports changed list
Host provisioning / Sync — consume bangbooPath and hollowPath to invoke the installed CLIs

harness-registration.summary: This layer wires the bangboo MCP server into the agent harnesses installed on the machine (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Cursor, Desktop, OpenCode). It is built as a table of per-harness adapters sharing one shape: detect presence, register, unregister, and check registration. The key idea is that each harness stores its server list its own way, so registration prefers each harness's own command and only edits config files directly where no command exists, with backups taken first.

flows.name: Register bangboo with a harness
steps: Detect which harnesses are present on PATH or via config paths
Resolve the installed bangboo binary path
Prefer the harness's own add/register command where one exists
Otherwise read, merge, and rewrite its JSON config with backup

flows.name: Unregister bangboo
steps: Run the harness's own remove command where available
Otherwise remove the bangboo entry from its config file

files: harness.go — harness table plus per-harness present/register/unregister/registered adapters, config paths, and backup helpers
rules: Where a harness has its own server-management command, use it rather than hand-editing its config.
Never overwrite a harness config without backing it up first.
Detection is by presence (binary on PATH or config file exists); do not register into harnesses that are not installed.
Config paths are OS-specific (e.g. Claude Desktop on darwin vs linux); keep the platform switch intact.
edges: CLI — install/uninstall subcommands drive register/unregister across all detected harnesses
Local install — supplies the bangboo binary path that gets registered
Runtime — registered harnesses launch bangboo as an MCP server to drive desks/hosts

host-provisioning.summary: This layer provisions remote (or local) machines as hollow hosts and remembers them in stateDir()/hosts.json. hosts.go owns the managed map and the `host add/ls/rm` commands; remote.go is the only transport — shell scripts run over ssh (or locally) plus hollow binary install and URL discovery. `host add` now also accepts a desktop connect code, creating a served-desktop host (NAME/desktop) that sync and doctor leave alone, alongside ssh-installed VM hosts.

map.name: Served desktop hosts via connect code

flows.name: Host add
steps: Parse dest or connect code plus --port/--idle flags in hosts.go (hostAdd)
For a code, register the served desktop as NAME/desktop without ssh or install
For an ssh dest, build remote{} in remote.go (local vs ssh dest)
Send and install hollow binary as service with settings in /etc/hollow.env
Discover host URL for the configured port

files: hosts.go — managed{ssh,url,added} state, loadManaged/saveManaged on hosts.json, host add/ls/rm commands including connect-code desktop hosts
remote.go — remote{dest,host,local} type, ssh invocation with BatchMode/ConnectTimeout/accept-new, script runner, hollow install and URL discovery
hosts_test.go — unit tests for host-settings logic, generated shell run against temp file under dash and nested sh -c quoting
rules: Hosts are reached over ssh and nothing else — any makima/Tailscale name, address, or ~/.ssh/config alias works; nothing is preinstalled remotely, phaethon ships hollow.
ssh always uses BatchMode=yes, ConnectTimeout=10, StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new; do not add interactive auth.
hosts.json lives under stateDir() with dir 0700 / file 0600 and shape {"hosts": {name: {ssh,url,added}}}; tolerate missing or malformed file as empty.
Local destination bypasses ssh entirely (sh -c directly); keep local and remote paths distinct.

Per-host port/idle live in /etc/hollow.env, not hardcoded (hollow always listens where told via env); --port must change both the service and the URL given to bangboo, upgrades must carry settings forward including moving legacy unit-file idle into the env file, and wait until the host answers as the new version instead of a fixed sleep.
Served desktops added via connect code are not ssh hosts: sync and doctor must leave them alone.
edges: CLI — cmdHost add/ls/rm entrypoint dispatches here from main.go
Bundle — hollow binary payload this layer sends and installs remotely
Sync and health — reads hosts.json state and discovered URLs to run bangboo host ls / doctor; sync preserves per-host settings on upgrade

sync-health.summary: Sync and health layer keeps managed hosts usable via `phaethon sync/doctor/scan`, driven by `bangboo host ls --json` output parsed into hostRow. It is built in a single file (sync.go) around hostRows, linuxImage inspection, and ensureImage rebuild/upgrade logic. Newcomers must grasp: upgrades preserve each host's port/idle settings and wait until the host answers as the new version, a current Linux image is left alone — only missing, failed, or outdated-recipe images trigger a rebuild — and sync can upgrade hosts set up through the bangboo library, not just `phaethon host add`.

flows.name: Ensure host image
steps: Run bangboo host ls --json via hostRows
Wait until host answers as new version instead of fixed sleep

files: sync.go — hostRow parsing, linuxImage check, settings-preserving ensureImage rebuild/upgrade with wait-for-answer, and sync/doctor/scan commands
rules: Never rebuild a current Linux image; only missing, failed, or older-recipe ones.
Linux image lookup matches on OS == linux; absence means state missing.

Host truth comes from bangboo host ls --json, not local state; a row whose backend is "desktop" (another machine desktop, bangboo local serve) runs no hollow and has no images, so sync and doctor report it answering and skip upgrades and image checks
Never hardcode port 7070 / idle 0 on upgrade; keep each host's existing settings including legacy unit-file idle moved into env.
After upgrading a host, wait until it answers as the new version, not a fixed 2s sleep.
doctor --deep must restore bangboo's remembered current desk when finished, and say so when no usable host exists instead of printing nothing.
edges: CLI — exposes this layer as sync/doctor/scan subcommands
Host provisioning — consumes its hosts.json/URL state via live host ls rows
Runtime — image rebuilds target x86_64 Linux KVM host images
Bundle — upgrades/images depend on bundled binaries and versions carried there
Bangboo library setup — sync upgrades hosts an app set up through bangboo, keeping port/idle/token
